title: Screen 50 Resumes Against Job Specs & Draft Tailored Interview Questions
oneLiner: Compare candidate resumes against job role requirements, spot real achievements versus buzzwords, and draft 5 tailored interview questions per candidate.
problem: Hiring managers spend hours reading generic resumes that look identical on paper. Standard interview questions yield canned answers, and it is difficult to spot whether a candidate actually owned a project or was just in the room.
workflow: Pasted the exact job description and must-have requirements into the agent context.
Uploaded candidate resumes in batches of 5.
The agent scored each resume on demonstrable evidence (not keywords) and produced a tailored 1-page interview cheat sheet with probing questions.
prompt:
You are an experienced technical hiring director. I have provided our target job description below:
[PASTE JOB DESCRIPTION HERE]

Now review the attached resume for [CANDIDATE NAME].

Generate an honest candidate brief containing:
1. Core Alignment (Score 1-10 with 2 bullet points of evidence from their actual track record).
2. Gaps or Red Flags (Missing critical skills or short unverified stints).
3. Five Custom Interview Questions designed specifically to test claims on their resume (e.g., 'You mentioned cutting cloud costs by 30%—what specific architecture changes did you implement?').
4. Recommendation: Advance to Screen / Reject / Need More Info.

realityCheck.firstTryMistake: The agent was initially too lenient with keyword stuffing until instructed to only give credit for quantified outcomes (numbers, percentages, dates).
realityCheck.manualCleanupTime: Zero cleanup needed for questions; required 2 minutes per candidate to review the scorecard.
realityCheck.limitations: Do not automate candidate rejection decisions entirely—always keep a human reviewer in the loop to prevent bias.
